newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGM problems.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGM problems.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Friday, led by a further surge in platinum and palladium prices, but pre-weekend position squaring reduced the gains across the complex near the close.
"There is extreme supply tightness which has virtually brought the physical market to a halt," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
"And NYMEX futures trade has been hampered by the lack of a basis in the cash market, like an engine without oil," he said.

The acute shortage of the white metals, caused by a suspension of Russian exports for five months, has forced shortcovering in the futures market and has seen a suspension of market making in forwards in the physical market.
In addition, the supply squeeze is resulting in delivery periods on spot physical transactions being negotiated out to 30 days, instead of the usual two days, to avoid defaults, traders said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $18.30 an ounce at $454.90, after seeing a new contract high at $473.80 early.
NYMEX warehouse platinum stocks fell 6,000 ounces to 60,000 ounces Thursday.
In the physical market, where quoted, spot platinum was indicated around $465.00 an ounce at the close, after seeing a morning high at $500.00, the highest level since 1990.
NYMEX June palladium, which expires on June 25, closed up $13.85 an ounce at $214.00, after seeing a new contract high at $224.00 an ounce.
The more active September palladium contract gained $5.85 to $179.00.
In the physical market, spot palladium was indicated around $225.00 an ounce, after seeing a 17 year high earlier this week.
NYMEX warehouse stocks of palladium fell heavily overnight and now just cover the amount of remaining open interest in June palladium contract which expires on June 25.
NYMEX warehouse palladium stocks fell 20,500 ounces to 32,200 ounces, while NYMEX June palladium open interest Thursday fell 37 lots to 325 contracts, representing 32,500 ounces of palladium.

Exchange officials said Friday deliveries on the June contract were proceeding normally, but some refiners reported difficulties. But NYMEX nearly doubled the deposit margins required on its platinum and palladium contracts from Monday.
In other other news, German catalytic converter maker Degussa AG, warned production curbs were possible in another three to four weeks if the supply squeeze continues.
Degussa produces about 20 percent of the world's catalytic converters, which automobile manufacturers use to filter pollution from automobile emission systems.
Meanwhile, relief was unlikely from South Africa, which produces about 60 percent of the world's platinum.
"I don't believe South African producers have stocks of metal," said Barry Davison, the managing director of Amplats, the world's largest supplier.
"I don't think relief can come from here. The relief can only come from a resumption of Russian supplies and dishoarding of the metal."
Russia produces about 20 percent of the world's platinum and about 60 percent of its palladium.
German bank Dresdner on Friday called on the U.S. Defense Stockpile to release some of the 431,000 ounces of platinum and the 1.264 million ounces of palladium it holds to ease the squeeze.
But the Stockpile's manager, Peter Roman, said Thursday Congressional approval was needed for another sale and it could not be organized before the end of summer.
Earlier this year the Stockpile sold 10,000 ounces of platinum and 15,000 ounces of palladium from the U.S. strategic reserve.

Russian officials told Japanese traders Wednesday that Russian PGM exports would resume on June 20, but Friday the head of the precious metals division of Russia's Finance Ministry warned platinum group metal (PGM) exports to Japan in 1997 would be a little below the levels seen last year.
The supply squeeze has been exacerbated by hedge fund accumulation of the metal also, analysts said.
New York based Tiger Management is believed to have acquired a stockpile of about 1.5 million ounces of palladium, representing about 20 percent of 1996 world palladium supply.
Meanwhile, COMEX August gold ended up 10 cents an ounce at $347.70 an ounce, after seeing a session high at $347.60, helped by the rise in PGM prices.
In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $343.20/70, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $344.00 and the New York close Thursday around $343.10/60.
COMEX July silver ended up 1.3 cents at $4.783, after seeing a high at $4.930 early.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 859-1641))
